name: Dark Peacock
lede: Dark Peacock is a deep, greenish blue named for the peacock's feathers, listed in our data only through a Japanese traditional color source and nearly matched by two other library names.

sections.title: A bird's name, thinly recorded
sections.body:
Our naming data classes Dark Peacock as a plant-and-landscape word, after the bird rather than a pigment or a place [1]. Unlike most of its neighbors it is not recorded in Ridgway's 1912 atlas or the ISCC-NBS lists of 1955; our only traced source for it is a Japanese traditional color list, undated in that source [1]. The ISCC-NBS classification that its hex would fall into is "moderate greenish blue," about 4.7 units from that block's center, even though no ISCC-NBS entry carries this exact name [1].

Two names in our data sit close enough to read as nearly the same color: [[venezia|Venezia]], 2.5 units away, and [[pearl-gentian|Pearl-Gentian]], 2.7 units away, both called "almost the same" in our computed comparison [2]. In LCH terms Dark Peacock measures lightness 27, chroma 36, hue 227 degrees: dark, moderately saturated, and between blue and green [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a close match covers enough of the canvas in 33, as photographed, rarer than 56 percent of the named colors we track [3]. It peaks in paintings from the 1900s, at 2.3 times the rate expected from that century's share of the archive [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays a hidden color, in a third of its matches, by lightness rank within the canvas [3]. The earliest match is a 1500 painting by Quentin Massys, as photographed, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3].
